pr.title: feat(desktop): Review v2 stage 1 — GitHub slice and Keryx links
pr.body:
Desktop Review v2, stage 1 "GitHub slice and links" (Flow 517): the Pull requests and Issues boards group by GitHub data only, every card gets a Keryx work row, and sessions can be bound to a PR or Issue. Three review rounds are done and their findings fixed; owner choices and known gaps are listed below. Requirements: `docs/requirements/keryx-desktop-review-v2/` (PRD R1–R3, R5, R6, parts of R4 and R7; decisions D5, D6). Stage 0 was #1294. Current state and deviations: section "Состояние этапа 1" of `implementation-plan.md`.

## What changes

- **Pull requests board, GitHub only (R1, R2, D6).** Groupings "Status" (default: Draft · Waiting for review · Changes requested · Approved; Merged and Closed only when the state filter includes them) and "My role" (Requested from me · Mine · Others). Quick filters "Requested from me", "Mine", "CI failed" sit in the context row, so the stage 0 toolbar measurements still hold. The attention and "In review" lanes are gone; the reason line uses GitHub data only.
- **Keryx work row (R4 part, R7 part).** A fixed 24px row on every PR card and list row with Review (`Review · <state>` from `localReview`, no round or behind count), Flow (by `prUrl` or a bound session's `flow` flag) and Session slots (count, newest, menu with all and "New session"). An empty slot shows its labelled action. "Fix review comments" is stage 4.
- **Sessions bound to a Subject (R5).** `subject` `{kind, repo, number, url, repositoryId?}` in the session's `flags.json`, written through `_keryx/session_flags` under a per-session `flags.json.lock` (the ACP server waits for it without blocking other sessions; a write to a session already moved to the trash is refused and does not bring it back). "Open in session" reopens the newest bound session or creates and binds one, prefilling the PR URL without sending. The session header links to the PR or Issue and its Flow. Issue sessions get `subject` from `withIssueBinding`; sessions an older keryx bound without one are backfilled on the next open unless the person unlinked it, and after the first bind a failed backfill no longer stops the issue from opening.
- **Older keryx.** keryx stores a new session only after its first turn, so the notice "binding was not saved" appears after that turn at the latest; the session keeps working.
- **Work from a bound session (R6).** `/review` with no target preselects the bound PR. "Create Flow" opens the bound session with a prefilled flow prompt. When exactly one new flow package appears within 15 minutes while exactly one request with a filled prompt is pending, the PR work row asks "Link Flow #N · <title>?" with Link and Dismiss. Only Link writes the session's `flow` flag; the offer stays until that write succeeds and shows why it failed. Dismiss, several new packages or several pending requests link nothing (AC9 as re-frozen in round 2).
- **Issues (R3, D5).** Default source "Project repository" (`keryx issues list` with `source: "repository"`, `/repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues`, pull requests dropped, up to 3 pages per load); a stored choice wins, and the choice is stored per project and account. Lanes Open · Closed by GitHub state. The Flow stage filter is gone; the work row has Flow and Session slots ("Open in session"). If the repository source is unavailable (no GitHub.com remote, a remote that names no usable repository, Issues turned off → 410, or an older keryx), the board shows the reason and "Show issues assigned to me", plus an update hint for an older keryx; any other error keeps Retry.
- **PR header link.** A header link to a PR in a repository the board lists selects that repository. A link the board cannot show (another repository it does not list, or a PR missing from the loaded list, e.g. filtered out by state) shows a notice and is cleared, so nothing opens later on its own.

No Rust changes. User docs: `docs/docs/guides/desktop-issues.md`, `docs/docs/cli-reference.md` (`issues`, and `_keryx/session_flags` in the ACP section).

## Verification

At head (after fix round 3):

- `cd apps/desktop && bunx tsc --noEmit`: clean. `bun test src`: 1070 pass, 0 fail.
- Root `bunx tsc --noEmit -p .`: clean. Root suites for the touched backend (`src/session/organize`, `src/acp/shell-session-organize`, `src/session/issues`, `src/integrations/issues-board`, `src/integrations/issues-launch`, `src/commands/issues`, `src/lib/file-lock`, `src/commands/acp`): 94 pass, 0 fail. `bun test src/acp`: 455 pass, 0 fail.
- Round 3 recorded runs (review package `research-evidence/`): the round's root and Desktop suites, and the verifier's repros of the three majors. Each fix in round 3 has a test that fails with the fix reverted (32 Desktop and 14 keryx checks, listed in the Flow 517 journal). The flags-lock tests no longer depend on elapsed time.
- The scenario "PR without Flow and review → Open in session → `/review` → review link on the card" is an App-level test.
- Stage 0 attention set: no line edited in any fix round.

Not verified: no run in the real app with real GitHub data; work row in narrow lanes, session menu placement, list width (1000px) and the LY-002/LY-004/LY-005 widths not measured; lint and the Rust CI path not run locally.

## Review

- Round 1 (head 6a2a3031f): 32 findings (2 blocker, 6 major); fixed in a34d8961b.
- Round 2 (head 88e3faba9): 44 findings (1 blocker, 3 major); HL-001 decided by the owner (confirmed link instead of a silent one); fixed in 80ef58bd5 and c4e8e3e24.
- Round 3 (head d7b0f7058, the round-2 fix range): 33 findings (0 blocker, 3 major, all confirmed by execution); fixed in 055115a20.
- Packages: `.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-23-review-flow-github-com-mrciphersmith-keryx-pull-1300`, `…-pull-1300-r02` and `.metaproject/reviews/2026-11-24-review-flow-github-com-mrciphersmith-keryx-pull-1300`. Decisions: the Flow 517 journal.

## Choices for the owner

Taken by the orchestrator during the fix rounds; each can be reverted:

- Create Flow waits 15 minutes from the press, not "until the next turn".
- A shown "Link Flow #N?" does not expire; Dismiss also stops offering that package. A failed Link is not retried after the turn; it waits for another press.
- A session switch while "Open in session" runs leaves no prompt and no pending request; a repeat press during an open reuses it without a prompt.
- New PR sessions also count a Flow found through a bound session; the launch dialog preselects the newest of several Flows.
- Review progress shows only in the slot title; the "Transcript updated" stamp left the card.
- A header link to a PR in a repository the board lists selects that repository; one the board cannot show gets a notice and is cleared.
- Warn tone for "needs answer" and "publication pending"; a merged PR keeps the "publication pending" text without the warn tone.
- "Show issues assigned to me" appears whenever the repository source is unavailable for one of the named reasons, chosen or not, and stores Assigned to me for this project only.
- Issues load up to 3 GitHub pages when a page holds only pull requests.
- A flags write waits up to 3 s for the lock, then fails with "retry".
- Subject backfill can re-link once a session unlinked before this version (no unlink marker then).
- In a very narrow lane the Flow slot clips the offer's Dismiss instead of overlapping the Session slot.
- Earlier UI choices: review slot state words; disabled "Run review" on merged or closed PRs; session menu button "More"; "not saved yet" for an unsaved session; "Create Flow" replaces the composer draft; Issue card buttons became work-row links.

## Known gaps

- Deviation (a), team review requests for the tab indicator, stays open; (b) is unchanged until stage 2.
- An Issue has no "another or new session" choice: the binding backend keeps one session per issue and account.
- A Flow created outside the Create Flow window, or with two or more requests pending, is not offered; it shows on the PR once it has a `prUrl`.
- `subject` names no GitHub account, so issue sessions bound under different accounts count together. GitHub Enterprise issues get no `subject`.
- A keryx older than this version drops `subject` and the unlink marker when it rewrites `flags.json`, so the next Issues open can re-link a subject the person unlinked (LG-014).
- Deferred info findings:
  - round 1 package: AR-002, PF-002, LG-004, LY-002/LY-004, UX-003..005;
  - round 2 package: PF-006/HW2-002, AR-004..006, HL-003, LG-014, LG-016, UX-006;
  - round 3 package: HL3-003, HL3-004, LG-R3-003, UX-014, UX-016, and SC3-001 (a stale-lock takeover race in the shared `src/lib/file-lock.ts`, which predates this PR; a separate change).

Flow package: `.metaproject/flows/517-2026-11-23-desktop-review-v2-stage-1-github-slice-a/`. Still to do: the merge decision.

entries.title: gdctx-flag-allowlist-no-bundle-expansion
entries.summary: A per-flag string allowlist that doesn't expand POSIX-bundled short flags rejects the idiomatic form of a tool's own CLI habits (`-il` vs `-i -l`); expand-then-check, not check-then-reject, for any allowlisted boolean-flag set.

entries.title: Findings reach a review round through the report's keryx:findings block, and a round without one silently records none
entries.summary: `keryx review ingest --report <md>` reads structured findings from a fenced ` ```json keryx:findings ` block inside the report. A report without that block ingests as `findings: in=0`, and every `--verifications` claim naming one of its findings is then discarded as unresolvable — because the finding it names is not in the round.

entries.title: keryx-gdctx-gdgraph-routing-index-cost-not-measured-before-shipping
entries.summary: A mandatory context-injection rule's per-read cost multiplies by every subsequent turn and every subagent dispatch. Measure the re-billed cost across a realistic turn count and subagent fan-out before setting a rule's default scope, not just its one-time size.

entries.title: The keryx on PATH is a stale build; the review pipeline does not exercise the code under review
entries.summary: `~/.local/bin/keryx` is an installed build, and its version lags the working tree. It is NOT the working tree. Every `keryx …` invocation — including `keryx review ingest`, which is how a managed review package is recorded — runs that build, so the review pipeline routinely does not exercise the code being reviewed.

entries.title: A fix round needs its own review: three consecutive rounds each introduced a blocker
entries.summary: On PR #215 (flow 127, project registry) three consecutive review-fix rounds each introduced a new blocker while closing the previous one. The defect was not in any single fix; it was in treating a fix as finished once it addressed the reported symptom.

entries.title: Theme switch repaints already-rendered chrome via old-slot value matching
entries.summary: `/theme` in the OpenTUI shell applied and persisted correctly on 0.2.66, but `applyTheme` (src/tui/shell-chrome.ts) only recolored the chrome's OWN surfaces (renderer background, sidebar border, docks, composer, `/`-menu). Every renderable painted EARLIER with `getTheme()` — transcript frames (user echoes, code-segment boxes, block bodies, side-worker boxes), tone-colored block headers (`theme.error`/`theme.tool`), dock/queue-dock buttons, sidebar panels — kept the old palette's hex in its `borderColor`/`backgroundColor`/`fg` props, so a dark→dark switch (groknight↔tokyonight) looked like "the theme did not apply". Fix: on every `applyTheme`, walk the renderable trees (transcript, docks, sidebarTop, menu, composer, header, footer) and rewrite any prop whose color equals an OLD theme slot hex to the NEW slot hex.

entries.title: A shell allowlist matched against the raw command string is not a security boundary
entries.summary: A remembered glob pattern that is matched against a command string which is then handed to `/bin/sh -c` grants far more than it appears to. The pattern matches text; the shell re-interprets that text. Verified, not theorised: a live allowlist contained `bash *`, `python3 *`, `curl *`, `cd *`, `# *`, `docker *`, `sudo *`, and the exact string `rm -rf /` — each an arbitrary-execution grant that auto-approved with no prompt.

finding.problem: The round-2 fix refuses a focus for a repository the board cannot show, but the sibling early return for a card absent from the loaded snapshot of the right repository still leaves the request armed with no notice. The header PR link (App setReviewFocus from SessionSubjectLinks) fires for any PR-bound session, including merged or closed PRs, and the board's default state filter is ["open", "draft"], so the card is absent.
finding.impact: Clicking the header link of a session bound to a merged PR switches to Pull requests and opens nothing, with no message. When the user later changes the state filter to include Merged, or the card appears in a later snapshot, the PR panel opens without being asked. This is the outcome LG-009 reported, through the other early return.
finding.suggested_fix: When a fresh (not stale, not loading) snapshot of the focused repository lacks the PR, set focused.current, show a notice (e.g. '#N is not in the current filters' with a 'Show all states' action) and call onFocusHandled(nonce). Keep waiting only on a stale cached snapshot.
finding.evidence: ReviewBoard.tsx:490-511 at head (the comment states the intent of not leaving a request armed); App.tsx:648-656 (header link sets focus for any PR subject); model.ts:28 EMPTY_FILTERS state ["open","draft"].

class_scope.enumeration_method: Every return in the single useEffect that consumes `focus` (ReviewBoard.tsx:496, 497-506, 508): :496 is a legitimate wait for the load, :497-506 was fixed in this range, :508 is still armed. `focus` has no other consumer.

finding.problem: Controls added in this range unmount themselves when activated and set no focus target: FlowOffer Link/Dismiss (the offer is dropped and the slot re-renders as a different button), the focus-notice 'Dismiss notice' button in ReviewBoard.tsx (the banner is removed), and 'Show issues assigned to me' in IssuesBoard.tsx (the source change remounts Collection by key). The sibling partial-sync dismiss in ReviewBoard.tsx already returns focus (warningToggle.current?.focus()).

finding.problem: withFlagsLock waits through lib/file-lock withFileLock, which spins in Bun.sleepSync(15) until it gets the lock. The caller is the long-lived ACP server's `_keryx/session_flags` handler (server.ts handleSessionFlags → setSessionFlags → updateSessionFlagsAt). A lock left by a writer killed mid-section therefore blocks the server's event loop for up to about 2 s (staleMs). An unremovable lock blocks it for the full 3 s timeout on every write.
finding.impact: While the server waits, the running turn's session/update stream, cancel and permission answers stall. Desktop writes flags without any user action (PendingSubjects.apply at turn end, Link on a Flow offer). The PR body accepts that a 'flags write may wait up to 3 s'; it does not say the whole server freezes.
finding.suggested_fix: On the ACP server path, wait asynchronously. Either make setSessionFlags/updateSessionFlagsAt async on top of lib/fs withFileLock, or try the O_EXCL create once synchronously and fall back to an async retry loop (await sleep(15)) until the deadline. Keep the synchronous form for the short-lived issue-workspace child only.
finding.evidence: src/session/organize.ts withFlagsLock (FLAGS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS 3_000, FLAGS_LOCK_STALE_MS 2_000); src/lib/file-lock.ts sleepSync uses Bun.sleepSync and the wait loop runs until the deadline; src/acp/server.ts calls setSessionFlags synchronously in the session_flags handler. finding.problem: On base, reopening an already bound issue session (stage session_bound or later, action open-session) did no flags.json I/O: bindIssueSubject ran only in the registered branch. On head it runs on every open-session and prepare-flow. backfillSessionSubject takes the flags lock and throws when it cannot: 'the flags of session X are locked by another keryx process; retry' after 3 s, or a write error. Nothing in withIssueBinding catches it, so the whole open fails before saveBinding and apply. The subject is a public decoration; the private binding record stays the authority (bindIssueSubject's own doc). An open that worked on base without touching flags can now be refused because of them. If true: major. The person cannot open the issue's bound session from the Issues board while the flags lock cannot be taken or flags.json cannot be written, for example an unremovable leftover flags.json.lock, a read-only session dir or no free inodes. The same open succeeds on base.
finding.impact: It applies only when the flags lock or file is unusable for more than 3 s. The trigger is environmental, which is why this is a question and not a finding. prepare-flow already wrote flags on base (issues-launch.ts:116), so its failure condition is unchanged. Only open-session on a reused binding changed.
finding.suggested_fix: Check: on head and on base, bind an issue session, then `chmod 0500` its session dir (or create a flags.json.lock the process cannot remove), then run `keryx issue-workspace open-session` for that issue. Base opens. If head refuses, make the backfill best-effort outside the registered branch: catch and ignore the error, or skip it when the session already has a subject, and keep it fatal only on first bind as on base.
finding.evidence: base-diff. Base 88e3faba9 issue-session.ts called bindIssueSubject(dir, issue.ref) inside `if (launch.stage === "registered") { ... }`. Head calls it after `if (!existsSync(dir)) throw ...`, unconditionally. organize.ts withFlagsLock: `if (held === null) throw new Error(...)`. backfillSessionSubject calls withFlagsLock before it reads current, so the lock is taken even when a subject already exists. Refute attempt: read issues-launch.ts:91-122. The workspace action returns before withIssueBinding, so read-only loads are unaffected. prepare-flow already called setSessionFlags on base (line 116), so it has no delta. withIssueBinding has no try/catch around bindIssueSubject. The commit 80ef58bd5 text and the PR body record the backfill but give no reason it must be fatal. Not run (read-only, exec_budget 0).

finding.problem: Stale recovery is by lock-file age only, with a 2 s threshold (the shared default is 10 s). A holder whose read plus atomic write stalls for more than 2 s has its lock broken while it still runs. The nonce stops it from deleting the new holder's lock, but both read-modify-writes proceed, and one update can be lost.
finding.impact: The HW2-001 lost update returns whenever a holder stalls for more than 2 s. No concrete trigger is shown in this repository, so this is info.
finding.suggested_fix: Record the holder PID in the lock file and break it only when that PID is gone, or use the shared LOCK_STALE_MS (10 s). Either still fits the 3 s timeout if the PID check runs first.
finding.evidence: src/lib/file-lock.ts stale branch: `if (age !== undefined && Date.now() - age > staleMs) rmSync(lockPath)`. There is no PID check.

finding.problem: Stale takeover can admit two holders. (a) Two waiters stat the same stale lock; one removes it and takes a fresh lock; the other then removes that fresh lock on the strength of its earlier stat and takes its own. (b) A holder whose section outlives staleMs (2 s for flags.json: a paused process or a stalled disk) is broken and still completes its write; the nonce only stops it deleting the new lock. The helper is unchanged in this range; this PR makes flags.json writers depend on it with a 2 s stale window.
finding.impact: No attacker vector: every lock party is a same-user keryx process. Outcome under the trigger (a crashed holder plus two concurrent waiters interleaving within microseconds, or a holder paused past 2 s): one flag change (pin, archive, flow, subject) is silently lost, the residual of HW2-001. Rare and narrow.
finding.suggested_fix: Optional, track separately (the helper is shared with the project registry and the serve credential store): break a stale lock by renaming it to a unique name and re-checking its mtime/nonce before deleting, or acquire through link(2), so a waiter never removes a lock it did not stat.
finding.evidence: src/lib/file-lock.ts withFileLock: acquire `openSync(lockPath, "wx", 0o600)`; on failure `statSync(...)?.mtimeMs` then `rmSync(lockPath)` with no re-check between them; the finally removes only when `readFileSync(lockPath) === nonce`. organize.ts withFlagsLock passes `staleMs: FLAGS_LOCK_STALE_MS` (2_000). git log -- src/lib/file-lock.ts: 18f169be5, 05a9a8e36 (both before base).
